name: Czechia
tagline: Your IB skips the paperwork everyone else has to do
summary: Since 1 March 2025 an IB Diploma is exempt from nostrification in Czechia by law. That matters more than it sounds: a Danish studentereksamen is not on the automatic-equivalence list and would have to go through a regional authority or pay a university assessment fee, while your IB Diploma is simply accepted. The other thing to know is that studying in Czech is free for everyone, regardless of nationality — the fee depends on the language of instruction, not on your passport. English-taught tuition runs from around 500 euros a year at the agricultural university to 24,250 for medicine at Charles.
whyConsider: The IB Diploma is a statutory route to prove secondary education. No nostrification, and at Charles and CTU no assessment fee either — while everyone else pays 950 to 1,000 CZK and waits.

Study taught in Czech is free at public universities for everyone, whatever your nationality. If you were willing to reach B2 Czech through a foundation year, the whole system opens up at no tuition cost.

Several English-taught deadlines fall after IB results come out in early July — Charles 1st Faculty of Medicine closed on 5 September, Masaryk medicine and Palacký in July, VSB Ostrava and CTU FEL in August. You can apply on real grades, not predicted ones.

Masaryk runs its medicine entrance exam through Interstudium in Oslo, and that centre explicitly covers Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Charles Plzeň uses Göteborg. Palacký and Hradec Králové offer the exam fully online.

Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine waives its entrance exam for 35 IB points including TOK and EE with 19 from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and one of Maths or Physics — and it accepts predicted grades, the only Czech faculty in this guide known to do so.
Living costs are 500 to 800 euros a month, and Olomouc, Plzeň and Ostrava sit at the cheaper end of that.
watchOuts: There is no central application portal. Every university, and in practice every faculty, runs its own application with its own deadline, fee and exam. Fees range from 500 CZK to 285 euros.

Most 2027 deadlines are not published yet. The firm ones are Charles 2nd Faculty (applications 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027, exam registration 30 April 2027, Prague sittings 3 June and 22 July 2027), VSE International Business (open 1 November 2026, close 28 February 2027, documents 31 July 2027) and VSB Ostrava Materials Science (1 October 2026 to 31 January 2027). Everything else is last cycle projected forward.
Every tuition figure here is 2026/27 or earlier. Expect increases. Anglo-American University has already said prices are expected to rise 5 percent for students starting after 31 August 2026.

The nostrification exemption is new, so older pages — including some still-live university pages and the IBO's own entry for CTU — still say the IB needs nostrification. You will meet contradictory information. One Charles faculty page appears to say something different again; ask FSV UK directly if that is your faculty.

Charles 3rd Faculty of Medicine requires HL English among the three subjects for its exam waiver and does not say whether English B counts. If you are taking English B HL, query it before relying on that route.

None of these faculties lists an entrance-exam venue in Denmark. For Charles 2nd Faculty the nearest dated overseas sittings are London (2 July 2027) and Berlin (13 July 2027); Oslo is listed but has no 2027 date yet. Plan on London or Berlin, an online sitting, or travelling to Czechia.

Two Charles 2nd Faculty pages disagree with each other. Its key-dates page gives 2027 Prague sittings of 3 June and 22 July, while its entrance-exam exemption page - the one an IB candidate needs, and stamped as updated in September 2026 - still prints the 2026 waiver deadline of 30 April and the old sittings of 27 May and 15 July. Ask the study department for the 2027 waiver deadline rather than inferring it.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set per faculty, and the pattern for medicine is clear: HL Biology plus HL Chemistry, with the third subject varying. Charles 2nd Faculty accepts Maths (AA or AI) or Physics at either level. Masaryk requires Physics specifically. Charles 3rd Faculty requires HL English as the third. For maths and computer science at Charles MFF the requirement is grade 6 in HL Maths, either AA or AI, and your total score is not considered at all.
notes: The headline rule: section 48(4)(c) of Act No. 111/1998 Coll., inserted by Act No. 52/2025 Sb. and in force since 1 March 2025, accepts an IB Diploma from an authorised IB World School as proof of completed secondary education for bachelor's and long-cycle master's admission. No nostrification is required.

This is a real advantage over a Danish studentereksamen. The automatic-equivalence list covers the European Baccalaureate, the IB, and school-leaving certificates from Slovakia, Poland, Hungary, Slovenia and Germany. Denmark is not on it, so a studentereksamen would need either regional nostrification at 1,000 CZK or a university assessment at 950 to 990 CZK.

Charles University states the IB is automatically accepted by the faculty without an assessment fee. CTU says plainly that IB holders' documents do not have to go through assessment or standard nostrification and go straight to the faculty.
Masaryk names the IB Diploma as an acceptable qualification but still charges a 990 CZK recognition fee, and its Faculty of Science charges 900 CZK for foreign-diploma verification.

Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine: exam waiver for 35 points overall including TOK and EE, with 19 points from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and one of HL/SL Maths or Physics. Predicted grades are explicitly accepted. Waivers are competitive and capped at 25 in the IB, EB and Baccalauréat group.
Charles 3rd Faculty of Medicine: admission without entrance exam for a maximum of 25 students, needing HL Chemistry, HL Biology and HL English summing to at least 19.

Masaryk Faculty of Medicine: waiver for General Medicine only, not Dentistry, at 35 points overall including TOK and EE with 19 from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and HL or SL Physics. It says 'achieved' rather than 'achieved or predicted', so predicted grades appear not to count.
Anglo-American University accepts the IB at a minimum of 24 points and waives its English test for IB Diploma holders.
Charles University's IB institution code is 000147.
No Czech institution publishes an IB points-to-Czech-grade conversion table.

portal.name: None. The official national portal states there is no single central application form — each institution, and usually each faculty, runs its own. studyin.gov.cz has a searchable programme database.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, entrance exam in Prague - regular date
deadlines.notes: A genuine 2027 date. The written paper is 75 questions in 90 minutes - 20 biology, 20 chemistry, 20 physics, 15 logic - worth 225 points, with up to 90 more from an interview. Sitting it in Prague on this date means travelling before your IB results arrive.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, entrance exam in London
deadlines.notes: London on 2 July 2027 is one of the two dated overseas sittings nearest Denmark; the other is Berlin on 13 July. The London sitting falls four days before IB results are released on 6 July. The faculty publishes no registration deadline for its overseas sittings, so ask the organiser when you must sign up.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, entrance exam in Berlin
deadlines.notes: Run through the agency Medical Doorway, and with London (2 July 2027) the nearest dated sitting to Denmark - reachable in a day. Oslo, nearer still, has no date yet. Unlike the Prague sittings, the faculty publishes no registration deadline for Berlin, so ask the agency when you must sign up.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, entrance exam in Prague - alternative date
deadlines.notes: The second Prague sitting, and the one that falls after IB results are released on 6 July 2027. You still have to register for it by 30 April.

deadlines.label: VSE Prague, Bachelor of International Business - hard copies of secondary-education documents
deadlines.notes: The deadline that decides whether an IB candidate can actually take the place up. VSE requires the physical documents by "31st July, 2027", stated twice on its required-documents page. IB results are issued on 6 July 2027, which leaves about three weeks to obtain, certify and post the diploma. One older page on the same site, last updated nine months earlier, says "at the latest by 1st July" - the two disagree; go by the later page, but confirm with the programme office before relying on either.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, overseas entrance exam sittings
deadlines.notes: The faculty lists about twenty overseas locations for 2027. The dated ones nearest Denmark are London (2 July 2027) and Berlin (13 July 2027), each with its own entry here; the others with dates are further away - Dubai, Tel-Aviv, Doha, New Delhi and Bangkok. Oslo, run through EduPlanet and the nearest sitting of all, is still "TBA", as are Frankfurt, Vienna, Munich, Vechta, Lisbon, Athens, Limassol, Istanbul, Toronto and Seoul. The page warns "Dates will be updated soon." and was last updated on 23 September 2026. No overseas registration deadline is published - the registration column exists only for the Prague sittings.

deadlines.label: Charles 2nd Faculty of Medicine, IB entrance exam waiver
deadlines.notes: The waiver is the most IB-specific thing this faculty offers and its 2027 dates do not exist. The exemptions page, stamped as last updated 21 September 2026, still carries the previous cycle throughout: apply and pay the 2,500 CZK fee "by 30 April 2026", notification "by the end of May 2026", and fallback Prague sittings on "27 May or 15 July" - dates that contradict the faculty's own 2027 key-dates page, which gives 3 June and 22 July 2027. The thresholds are stated and are presumably stable: at least 35 points including EE and TOK, at least 19 from HL Biology and HL Chemistry together, plus HL or SL Maths or Physics, with a maximum of 25 waivers shared across the IB, EB and BS group. Ask the study department for the 2027 waiver deadline rather than inferring it.

deadlines.label: Palacky University Olomouc, General Medicine in English - 2027 entrance examination dates
deadlines.notes: Not published: the faculty's table is headed "Entrance examination dates and venues for 2026" and has not rolled over. Two features of the 2026 list matter enough to carry forward. First, four sittings late in the season - 18, 19, 25 and 28 August 2026 - were marked as open only to applicants who are EU citizens or hold a valid residence permit, which is an advantage you have as an EU citizen and a non-EU candidate does not. Second, the examination can be taken only once per academic year, so the date you pick is the only attempt you get.

deadlines.label: VSB Technical University of Ostrava, Faculty of Economics - 2027/28 admission rounds
deadlines.notes: The Faculty of Economics does not publish a five-round structure. Its own admissions page sets out three bachelor rounds, and those are for the Czech-taught programme; the number five appears only as a label on one row of the university dates table, "5. kolo" against the 2026/27 English-taught bachelor intake, which opened 5 August and closed 14 August 2026. The table only ever shows the currently open round per programme, so earlier rounds are never visible. Nothing at all is published for 2027/28, and the faculty pages are imperfectly maintained - one section prints 2025 document deadlines against its own 2026 round dates.

deadlines.label: Charles University, English-taught programmes
deadlines.year: 2026/27 pattern; no faculty has published 2027/28 dates
deadlines.notes: The central page carries only a range - English-taught bachelor's and master's deadlines "vary for each faculty (from February till June/July)" - and it is stamped as last changed in May 2023, so it is three years stale and names no faculty. Mathematics and Physics closed 30 April 2026; the Third Faculty of Medicine 15 April 2026; Plzen 30 April 2026; Hradec Kralove works differently, with 30 April 2026 for its online sitting and 7 May 2026 for sittings held abroad rather than one global deadline; and the First Faculty of Medicine ran to 5 September 2026. None has published anything for 2027/28. Judging by this cycle, expect them from November or December 2026, faculty by faculty, on each faculty's own site rather than centrally. Charles also states that it has no rolling admissions and grants no individual extensions.

deadlines.label: Anglo-American University
deadlines.notes: Published as "We have rolling admissions, therefore, you can submit your applications all year round." A realistic safety option if your plans change late. The application fee is 1,000 CZK and the admissions office says it decides one week after your interview, so the turnaround is short as well as the deadline absent.

steps: Work out which faculty you want, not just which university. In Czechia the faculty sets the fee, the deadline, the exam and the IB rules, and they differ enormously inside one institution.

Check whether your target faculty offers an IB-based exemption from the entrance exam. At Charles 2nd Faculty and Masaryk this can remove the exam entirely, and at Charles 2nd Faculty predicted grades count.
Apply directly to each faculty through its own system, during autumn 2026 or early 2027. Most windows open between October and January.
Pay the application fee, which ranges from 500 CZK at the agricultural university to 285 euros at Charles 1st Faculty of Medicine.
Tick the box declaring that you hold an IB Diploma so the faculty applies the section 48(4)(c) route and does not charge you an assessment fee.

Book your entrance exam at the nearest workable venue. For medicine that realistically means Oslo through Interstudium for Masaryk, Göteborg for Charles Plzeň, an online sitting at Palacký or Hradec Králové, or London (2 July) or Berlin (13 July 2027) for Charles 2nd Faculty.

If your results come out better than expected in early July, look again at the faculties that are still open — Charles 1st Faculty, Masaryk medicine, Palacký and VSB Ostrava all accept applications after results day.
Once admitted, register your stay within 30 working days of arriving, unless your dormitory handles it for you, and apply for a hall place immediately because places are limited and not guaranteed.
application.selectionNotes: Almost every programme runs its own entrance exam. Medicine is typically a written multiple-choice paper in biology and chemistry plus a third subject, followed by an interview: Charles 1st Faculty uses five multiple mini-interviews of ten minutes each; Charles 2nd Faculty asks 75 questions in 90 minutes and then interviews the top scorers; Masaryk sets three separate 50-minute papers with a 60 percent pass mark for General Medicine. Caps are tight — around 90 places at Charles 2nd and 3rd Faculties, 105 at Hradec Králové, about 80 at Palacký. Outside medicine, CTU's Faculty of Information Technology runs a maths test or accepts SCIO online tests, CTU's Faculty of Electrical Engineering uses an online interview, and VŠE's International Business has no written test at all — just an online interview scored 50 points for motivation and 50 for English.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Wide, but concentrated. Study in Czechia quotes more than 1,000 degree programmes in English across all levels (2023 figure). At bachelor's level, verified counts include VŠE with 8 (two of them opening in September 2027), UCT Prague with 8, Czech University of Life Sciences with 10, Masaryk with around 11, the Academy of Performing Arts with 3, Brno University of Technology with effectively 1, and West Bohemia and South Bohemia with 1 each. Charles and CTU publish no bachelor's-only count.
language.englishProof: Varies widely. Charles MFF accepts IB English at grade 6, or IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 85. Anglo-American University waives the test for any IB Diploma holder. VŠE's International Business requires no certificate at all and assesses English inside the interview. Charles 1st Faculty of Medicine required no English certificate at all for 2026/27. CTU's Faculty of Electrical Engineering wants TOEFL iBT 70, IELTS 6 or TOEIC 800 and does not accept Duolingo. Palacký wants Cambridge FCE, IELTS 6, TOEFL 87 or PTE 59, or its own test, unless your secondary education was in English.
notes: Study taught in Czech is free at public and state institutions regardless of nationality — that is written into section 58(1) of the Higher Education Act. Most Czech-taught programmes want at least B2 Czech, reachable in about a year through an intensive foundation programme, and that is a genuinely serious option if cost matters more than speed.

Medical students on English-taught programmes still have to learn Czech for clinical work. Masaryk sets compulsory Czech exams at the end of years one, two, three and four, and Charles 3rd Faculty requires Czech proficiency by the end of year two.

An IB Diploma taught in English satisfies most institutions, but the accepted form differs: some want your IB English grade, some accept the diploma outright, and some want a separate certificate anyway.

tuitionEuEea.value: Free if you study in Czech. For English-taught bachelor's degrees: Czech University of Life Sciences 500 euros a year at its Faculty of Engineering (2025/26), Brno University of Technology 1,000 euros (2026/27), Masaryk 3,000 euros for most science programmes up to 14,000 for Data Analytics, UCT Prague 84,500 CZK with the entry-year rate locked for the whole degree, Charles MFF 4,200 euros, VŠE 5,000 euros, CTU 110,000 to 128,000 CZK depending on faculty, VSB Ostrava about 4,000 euros, West Bohemia 3,000 to 4,000, Anglo-American University 125,489 CZK a semester. English-taught medicine: Palacký Olomouc 12,500 euros a year, Masaryk 380,000 CZK, Charles Plzeň 390,000 CZK, Charles 2nd and 3rd Faculties 420,000 CZK, Charles 1st Faculty 24,250 euros.
tuitionEuEea.year: mostly 2026/27; CZU 2025/26; South Bohemia's range is 2023/24 and stale

tuitionNonEu.value: Often the same, but not always — several universities give EU citizens a lower rate. Verified gaps: Charles MFF 4,200 euros for EU against 7,100 for non-EU; Brno University of Technology 1,000 against 4,500; Czech University of Life Sciences 500 against 1,000; Anglo-American University 125,489 CZK a semester against 144,404. The medical faculties at Charles, Masaryk and Palacký publish a single figure per programme with no nationality split, but none of them states equality in so many words.

costs.applicationFee: No national rule — it varies by faculty. Verified: 500 CZK at CZU and West Bohemia, 600 at VSB Ostrava, 700 at Brno University of Technology, 800 at Masaryk's Faculty of Science, 940 at Charles 3rd Faculty and Plzeň, 950 at CTU, 1,000 at Anglo-American University, 1,500 at Charles MFF, 2,500 at Charles 2nd Faculty and Hradec Králové, 80 euros at Palacký, 100 euros for VŠE International Business and 285 euros at Charles 1st Faculty.

livingCostMonthly.value: 500 to 800 euros a month for basic living. Food and drink 150 to 230; a student canteen meal 4 euros; a yearly student transport pass 50 to 100 euros. Prague sits at the top of the range and Olomouc, Plzeň and Ostrava at the bottom — a city-centre flat is 1,060 euros in Prague, 870 in Brno and around 620 to 635 in Olomouc, Plzeň and Ostrava.

notes: The whole fee structure turns on language, not nationality. Section 58(1) of Act No. 111/1998 says study at a public higher education institution in Czech is free of charge, and section 58(5) lets institutions set foreign-language fees with no cap — which is why English-taught prices vary from 40 euros to over 30,000.
Czech-taught study only becomes chargeable if you exceed the standard duration by more than a year. At Masaryk that costs 24,000 to 51,000 CZK per six months depending on how far over you are.
Anglo-American University has flagged that prices are expected to rise 5 percent for new students starting after 31 August 2026, which covers this cohort.
Masaryk charges a 25,000 CZK cancellation fee if you pay tuition and then do not enrol.
UCT Prague locks your entry-year rate for the whole degree, which is unusual price certainty.
Every figure here is 2026/27 or earlier. No 2027/28 tuition fee was published anywhere as of September 2026.
Where euro figures sit next to CZK ones, the conversion is at roughly 25 CZK to the euro, the rate Charles 2nd Faculty itself publishes.

funding.note: In 2026 it is DKK 7,426 a month before tax if you live away from your parents. The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip). The cap does not cover a six-year medical degree.

funding: The biggest saving available is structural rather than a scholarship: study in Czech is free at public universities for everyone regardless of nationality. Reaching B2 Czech through a foundation year costs money and a year of your life, but it removes tuition entirely.

University-level aid exists at every institution but is set individually: merit scholarships, tuition waivers and reductions, and accommodation or emergency support. Masaryk lists eight separate sources.
Section 58 of the Higher Education Act lets a rector reduce, waive or defer study fees on academic or social grounds. It is a real safety valve worth asking about if your circumstances change.

Czech Government scholarships exist but are described only as being for students from selected countries, and the portal does not publish the list. Whether Denmark or any EU state qualifies is not confirmed here.
Erasmus+ covers exchanges and traineeships of two to twelve months once you are enrolled, and CEEPUS covers mobility within central and south-eastern Europe.
workRights: As an EU citizen you have the same access to the Czech labour market as a Czech citizen and need no work permit. There is no immigration-law cap on hours. The contract types matter more: a DPP agreement is capped at 300 hours a year per employer, a DPČ at about 20 hours a week, and a standard employment contract has no such limit. The minimum wage in May 2026 was 134.40 CZK an hour or 22,400 CZK a month, and student part-time work typically pays 150 to 200 CZK an hour.
residency: No visa and no residence permit. You enter on a valid passport or national ID card. If you are staying more than 30 days you must register within 30 working days of arriving — much gentler than the three working days non-EU students get. In practice the obligation often does not apply if your accommodation provider, such as a student dormitory, registers you, so confirm with your hall. Whether an EU student should also obtain the optional certificate of temporary residence is not confirmed here; ask your university.
housing: Halls of residence, called koleje, cost roughly 160 to 330 euros a month for a shared room and 250 to 450 for a single, with utilities and Wi-Fi often included. Places are limited and not guaranteed. At Charles the queue order matters: returning residents extend their contracts in May, international students who need a visa apply from mid-April, and the general electronic application only opens in mid-June — which puts EU students with no visa need in the last and most competitive queue. Apply the day it opens. A room in a shared private flat runs 250 to 500 euros a month. Prague and Brno are markedly more expensive than Hradec Králové, Olomouc or Liberec.
healthcare: Bring your EHIC. It gives you medically necessary care from public providers on the same terms as a Czech insured person. The national portal is clear that the EHIC is not travel insurance — it generally does not cover private clinics, repatriation or travel losses, so supplementary cover is sensible. Whether an EU student also needs to register with a Czech health insurer such as VZP is not addressed on the official pages; ask your university.

institutions.name: Charles University
institutions.englishBachelors: Not published as a bachelor's-only count. The university reports over 850 accredited programmes with more than 200 in languages other than Czech, across all levels.
institutions.note: Czechia's oldest and largest university, and organised so that the faculty matters more than the name. Its Faculty of Mathematics and Physics is the only one publishing an explicit IB grade rule — a 6 in HL Maths, with your total score ignored. Its five medical faculties each set their own fee, exam and IB waiver, ranging from 390,000 CZK a year in Plzeň to 24,250 euros at the 1st Faculty in Prague. Price and plan the faculty, not the university.

institutions.name: Masaryk University
institutions.englishBachelors: Around 11 — including Biology and Biochemistry, Data Analytics, English Language and Literature, Business Management and Finance, International Relations and European Politics, and Global Challenges. Plus General Medicine and Dentistry.
institutions.note: The broadest English-taught bachelor's menu outside Prague, priced from 3,000 to 14,000 euros depending on programme, and the one institution that runs its medicine entrance exam through a centre covering Denmark — Interstudium in Oslo, with dates in March, May, June and July. It also gives EU citizens the June and July exam slots that non-EU applicants cannot use, which means you can sit it after IB results. Its medicine waiver needs 35 points with 19 from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and Physics, and unlike Charles 2nd Faculty it appears not to accept predicted grades.

institutions.name: Czech Technical University in Prague
institutions.englishBachelors: Not published as a count — the official list is a PDF. English-taught bachelor's degrees exist at the Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Nuclear Sciences, Architecture, Transportation, Biomedical and Information Technology faculties.
institutions.note: One of Europe's oldest technical universities, and the clearest institution in Czechia on the IB: it states outright that IB holders skip both the rectorate assessment and standard nostrification, saving the 950 CZK fee. Note that fees differ sharply by faculty, from 110,000 CZK a year at Electrical Engineering to 128,000 at Information Technology. Its IT faculty lets you take either an in-person maths test or a SCIO test online; its electrical engineering faculty admits by online interview in August.

institutions.name: Prague University of Economics and Business
institutions.englishBachelors: 8 — Economics, Business Administration, International Business, International and Diplomatic Studies, Economics of Markets and Organizations, Economic Data Science, plus Finance and Accounting and Business Information Systems, both opening in September 2027
institutions.note: Two brand-new English-taught bachelor's degrees open in exactly the September 2027 intake this cohort enters — which means no track record, but also less competition. Its International Business programme has genuine 2027 dates already published and an unusual admission process: no written test, just an online interview scored half on motivation and half on English, with the five possible topics published in advance. No English certificate is required at all.

institutions.name: Palacký University Olomouc
institutions.englishBachelors: Not published as a count — it describes a wide range of English-taught programmes across eight faculties without giving a number.
institutions.note: The second-oldest Czech university and by far the cheapest English-taught medicine in the country at 12,500 euros a year, against 15,200 to 24,250 elsewhere. Most of its entrance exam dates are fully online, and EU citizens get extra terms in late August that non-EU applicants cannot use. The 80-euro application fee covers the exam. It publishes no IB exemption, only an English-test exemption if your education was in English.

institutions.name: Czech University of Life Sciences Prague
institutions.englishBachelors: 10 — Business Administration, Economics and Management, Informatics, Agriculture and Food, Sustainable Use of Natural Resources, Agricultural Engineering, Environmental Data Science, Environmental Engineering, Forestry, and International Cooperation in Agriculture and Rural Development
institutions.note: An English-taught bachelor's route at 500 euros a year for an EU student at the Faculty of Engineering in 2025/26, against 1,000 for non-EU students — and with a genuinely wide programme list rather than one token degree. Applications run 15 January to 31 March and the application fee is 500 CZK.

institutions.name: Brno University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Effectively 1 — Electrical Engineering, three years, with specialisations in electronics and communication technologies or in power systems and automation
institutions.note: Fees are 1,000 euros a year for EU students, against 4,500 for non-EU. The catch is that there is essentially one English-taught bachelor's programme, so it either fits you or it does not. Fees are payable in euros only, with proof due by 15 September.

institutions.name: University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague
institutions.englishBachelors: 8 — Catalysis and Manufacturing of (In)organic Compounds, Inorganic Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Materials, Physical and Computational Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, plus a business economics and management school
institutions.note: 84,500 CZK a year regardless of nationality, and unusually, the rate you enter on is locked for your whole degree — so you know your total cost on day one. A strong option if HL Chemistry is your subject and medicine is not your plan.

institutions.name: Anglo-American University
institutions.englishBachelors: Not published as a count. Programmes span business administration, international relations, humanities and journalism.
institutions.note: The first private university in the country to teach in English, and the only one here with rolling admissions and no deadline — which makes it a realistic safety option if your July results change the plan. It accepts the IB at 24 points and waives the English test for IB holders. It is also the most expensive on this list at 125,489 CZK a semester for EU students, roughly 10,400 euros a year, and has warned that prices are expected to rise 5 percent for students starting after August 2026.

institutions.name: VSB - Technical University of Ostrava
institutions.englishBachelors: Not published as a count. English-taught bachelor's degrees exist across seven faculties, with admission conditions varying by faculty.
institutions.note: Five admission rounds running into mid-August make Ostrava unusually forgiving for an IB student whose July results change things — and it has already confirmed that applications for 2027/28 open on 1 October 2026. Tuition is about 4,000 euros a year from 2026/27, and Ostrava is one of the cheapest cities in the country to live in.

institutions.name: University of West Bohemia
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Management and Digital Technology at the Faculty of Economics, run as a four-year double degree
institutions.note: One English-taught bachelor's route only, but it is a four-year double degree rather than a token offering, at 3,000 to 4,000 euros a year. Plzeň is also where Charles University's Faculty of Medicine in Plzeň sits, and that faculty runs an entrance exam venue in Göteborg — the closest to Denmark found anywhere.

institutions.name: Academy of Performing Arts in Prague
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Authorial Acting at the theatre faculty, Photography at FAMU, and Dance Pedagogy at the music and dance faculty
institutions.note: Home of FAMU, the world's fifth university-level film school, and the only conservatoire in Czechia with English-taught bachelor's degrees. Entry is by audition or portfolio. Its tuition fees are not published anywhere readable — you have to ask the International Department.

institutions.name: University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Biological Chemistry at the Faculty of Science, three years. The rest of its English catalogue is master's and doctoral.
institutions.note: A single English-taught bachelor's route, but a distinctive joint one with Johannes Kepler University in Austria — 20 places through South Bohemia plus further places through JKU. One odd instruction worth noting: accepted students are told to apply for visas in Austria rather than Czechia. Applications close at the end of March and are not accepted outside that window. Its published fee range is from 2023/24 and is out of date.
